speaker: narrator
text: He falls in his own house. What is left of him is dust, and for a moment the dust keeps a shape, kneeling.

speaker: narrator
text: Lenka stands with you, Anton's ring on its cord at her throat.

speaker: narrator
text: She does not look at the dust. She looks at the window, and the morning.

speaker: narrator
text: The Lantern's light finds Lenka where he kept her. The cold leaves her hands. She crosses the room to you on her own.

speaker: narrator
text: In the light stand two shapes, not quite there.

speaker: narrator
text: A young man with a sword like the one you carry. A woman holding violets. Then they are gone.

speaker: lenka
text: She told him no. So did I. Take me home.

speaker: narrator
text: Down in the valley, doors open. People stand in the street and look up at a sky they have not seen since spring.

speaker: narrator
text: The mist lifts off Vellmoor. The road out is there again, and nobody takes it today.

speaker: narrator
text: He falls in his own house. What is left of him is dust. The castle goes quiet around you, all at once.

speaker: narrator
text: You search for Lenka until the candles burn down. Every door opens for you now. Every room is empty.

speaker: narrator
text: In the room where he kept her, the window stands open. On the sill lie Anton's ring on its cord, and one pressed violet.

speaker: narrator
text: Below, the mist pulls back off the roads. The valley is free. Whether she is, no one can say.

speaker: narrator
text: He is gone, and the sun comes back to Vellmoor. You came for the burgomaster's daughter. You go home with his ring.

speaker: narrator
text: In every parish the doors stand open, and no one stands in them. The bells have stopped.

speaker: narrator
text: The people of Vellmoor walk up the hill through the mist, quiet, in their best clothes. None of them looks back.

speaker: narrator
text: At the castle, every window is lit. Somewhere above, someone is playing the organ.

speaker: narrator
text: The last skull falls. The mist closes over Vellmoor, and the valley is his for good.

speaker: narrator
text: The third bite is not the worst one. It is only the last. Somewhere a heartbeat stops, and another starts, slower.

speaker: narrator
text: A hunter goes very still. Then they turn, and walk out into the mist, toward the hill.

speaker: narrator
text: Nobody calls after them. On the hill, one more window is lit.

speaker: narrator
text: A hunter is his now. The hunt is over, and the mist stays down.

speaker: narrator
text: The fourth house falls. Its shutters hang open, and the garlic on its sills has gone black.

speaker: narrator
text: There is no door left in Vellmoor that will hold. From now on, someone is asked in, and goes.

speaker: narrator
text: Four houses have fallen. There is nowhere left to shut a door, and he walks in where he likes.
